criteria.name: Q1 Quality attributes
criteria.reasoning: Two attributes justified from scenario evidence (lunch peak, 4.2 s p95, payment outage). Both scenarios contain all six parts and both response measures are quantified and measurable.

evidence.quote: Performance and availability matter most: 900 orders arrive in the lunch hour, the 4.2 s p95 makes students abandon their orders
Response measure: menu p95 stays under 2 s, under 0.1% of non-payment requests fail, and ordering works again within 1 minute

criteria.name: Q2 Architectural style
criteria.reasoning: Clear modular-monolith recommendation with two scenario-specific trade-offs (team size/ops overhead; single VM and 20-minute downtime vs rewrite cost) and an explicit acknowledged downside.

evidence.quote: Five developers running eight or more services would spend more time on infrastructure than on features
The downside I accept is that modules cannot be scaled independently and a bug in one module can still crash the whole process

criteria.name: Q3 Availability calculation
criteria.reasoning: Series product 0.99301 (99.30%) correct; downtime 5.03→5.0 h correct; parallel payment 0.999975, combined 0.99798 (99.80%), downtime 1.46→1.5 h correct. Working shown, precision as requested.

criteria.name: Q4 Resilience pattern
criteria.reasoning: Circuit Breaker named, states and transitions explained correctly, applied to the 25-minute payment hang, with both a tuning consideration and a drawback (no payments while open, fallback needed).

evidence.quote: When failures exceed a threshold the breaker moves to Open and calls fail immediately, so request threads are not blocked
Tuning consideration: the threshold must come from real latency data

criteria.name: Q5 Consistency and availability
criteria.reasoning: AP for browsing and CP for payments, both justified; CAP used correctly (partition tolerance not optional); concrete techniques given (Redis TTL cache, idempotency key with rejection on partition).

evidence.quote: The CAP theorem says that during a partition a system must give up either consistency or availability
it is better to show a slightly stale menu from a cache (Redis with a 60-second TTL)

criteria.name: Q6 Architecture decision record
criteria.reasoning: Context, Decision and Consequences all present and scenario-specific, with two positive and three negative consequences (ops burden, at-least-once duplicates, premature 'paid' state).

evidence.quote: Context: After an order is paid, the application calls the outlet's tablet synchronously and waits for the reply
Consequences (negative): The queue is one more component for five developers to run and monitor

criteria.name: Communication and format
criteria.reasoning: All answers at or under 150 words, required headings in order, precise terminology, IEEE-style citations and reference list present.

evidence.quote: Each order request carries an idempotency key, so a retry does not create a second charge
[1] L. Bass, P. Clements, and R. Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice, 3rd ed.

technical_issues.issue: Rounding of 0.993011 to 99.30% and 5.03 to 5.0 h is correct; no error, but intermediate value 0.99301 slightly truncates (0.993011) — immaterial.
Idempotency key is a retry-safety mechanism rather than a partition-consistency technique per se; acceptable alongside the CP rejection choice but slightly loose.
No explicit assumptions section despite the brief requiring assumptions to be stated (e.g. independence of failures, 30-day month).

overall: Near-exemplary submission: all six questions answered in six-part/ADR form, calculations fully correct to the requested precision, trade-offs and drawbacks scenario-specific, and all answers within the 150-word limit with IEEE references. Only gap is the missing explicit assumptions statement.

feedback.summary: Your submission is near-exemplary: all six answers are complete, calculations are correct, trade-offs are scenario-specific, and writing is within limits with IEEE references. You justify choices clearly and acknowledge downsides. The only improvement is to add an explicit assumptions section (e.g., failure independence, 30-day month) so readers can see the basis for your calculations and scenarios.
next_steps: Add a short 'Assumptions' subsection before Q3 (and where relevant in Q1/Q5) stating independence of component failures, a 30-day month, and that response measures are under lunch-peak load; this closes the only gap noted in the overall marking.

In Q5, tighten the idempotency-key discussion: frame it explicitly as retry safety supporting your CP choice, and name a partition-consistency technique (e.g., quorum writes or rejecting writes during partition) so the technique maps directly to CAP.
Keep every answer at or under 150 words and preserve IEEE citations; when revising, re-check Q3 rounding to the requested precision (99.30%, 5.0 h, 99.80%, 1.5 h) and keep working shown.

criteria.C1: You chose performance and availability and grounded them in scenario evidence (900 orders/lunch hour, 4.2 s p95, payment outage). Both six-part scenarios are complete and your response measures are measurable (p95 <2 s, <0.1% non-payment failures, recovery <1 minute). This is Excellent; to maintain it, keep each part explicit and quantified.
criteria.C2: Your modular-monolith recommendation is clear and tied to the five-developer team and single-VM/20-minute downtime constraints. You give two scenario-specific trade-offs and explicitly acknowledge the downside (no independent scaling; one module can crash the process). Excellent level met; to sustain it, keep linking each trade-off to a named scenario fact.
criteria.C3: All three parts are correct with working shown: series product 0.99301 (99.30%), downtime 5.03→5.0 h; parallel payment 0.999975, combined 0.99798 (99.80%), downtime 1.46→1.5 h. Precision matches the request. Excellent; to keep it, continue showing intermediate values and state assumptions such as failure independence and 30-day month.
criteria.C4: You name Circuit Breaker, explain Open/Half-Open/Closed transitions correctly, and apply it to the 25-minute payment hang. You include a tuning consideration (threshold from real latency data) and a drawback (no payments while open; fallback needed). Excellent; to maintain, keep tying the pattern to the specific outage and naming the fallback behaviour.
criteria.C5: You choose AP for browsing and CP for payments, justify both, and use CAP correctly (partition tolerance is not optional). Techniques are concrete: Redis TTL cache for menus and idempotency key with rejection on partition for payments. Excellent; to tighten, frame idempotency explicitly as retry safety and pair the CP choice with a partition-consistency technique.
criteria.C6: Your ADR has Context, Decision and Consequences, all scenario-specific: synchronous tablet call, queue-based decision, and two positive plus three negative consequences (ops burden, duplicates, premature 'paid'). Excellent; to sustain, keep consequences balanced and explicitly label positive/negative as you did.
criteria.C7: All answers are within 150 words, headings are in order, terminology is precise, and IEEE citations/reference list are present. Excellent. To keep this level, add the brief assumptions statement the brief requires and re-check word counts after any revision; citations are already well formed.
